text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbian government says exports to reach $2.15 billion by the end of the year, up by 47 percent on 1995.
- Yugoslavia and Macedonia sign trade and economic agreements in Skopje
- Bor copper mines in eastern Serbia suffer over one million dollars in damages due to floods. Normalisation of production expected next week.
- President of the city government of Kragujevac Milorad Matic resigns over prolonged Zastava weapons factory pay protests.
- Provisional Election Commission (PEC) says 3,398 party and independent candidates will contest Bosnia elections.
- Russia has approved a $50 million commodity credit to Bosnian Serb republic covering all goods except oil and gas, says director of Moscow's Prometexport Belgrade office Alexandar Lesin.
- Yugoslavia could start exporting meat to EU countries early next year says secretary-general of EU livestock commission visiting Belgrade.

- Yugoslav and Italian officials agree in Milocer for a study to be drafted on Transbalkan gas pipline. Two versions considered - one from Romania via Bulgaria, Serbia and Montenegro to southern Italian port of Bari and the other via Albania to Brindisi.
- Transporter Lasta to open first Belgrade-Zagreb bus line on Sept 15.
